subject: Archaeology
title: The Invention of Clothing
description: Learn The Invention of Clothing in one minute.

hook.text: Clothes rot away. So how do archaeologists know when humans started wearing them? They studied lice.

buildup.text: Body lice evolved from head lice when humans started wearing clothes — giving lice a new habitat to colonize.

discovery.text: DNA analysis dates the split between head lice and body lice to about 170,000 years ago — the likely start of clothing.

twist.text: The oldest sewing needle is 50,000 years old, found in a Denisovan cave.

climax.text: Clothing was not about modesty. It was survival technology that let humans leave Africa and survive ice ages.

punchline.text: We figured out when humans got dressed by asking when lice moved in.

quiz.question: How did scientists determine when humans first wore clothing?
options: They carbon-dated the oldest preserved fabric fragments
They analyzed when body lice evolved from head lice using DNA
They found cave paintings depicting people wearing animal skins

details.summary: Humans began wearing clothing at least 170,000 years ago, based on genetic evidence from body lice that adapted to live in clothing. Early garments were animal hides sewn with bone needles, essential for survival as humans colonized cold northern environments.
details.whyItMatters: Clothing enabled human expansion into cold climates that would otherwise be uninhabitable. This technological innovation was as important as fire in allowing our species to colonize the entire planet.
takeaways: Clothing use dates to at least 170,000 years ago via lice genetics
Bone needles show sewing technology by 40,000 years ago
Clothing enabled colonization of cold climates worldwide

faq.question: How do lice reveal when clothing was invented?
faq.answer: Body lice evolved from head lice when humans started wearing garments, giving lice a new habitat. By calculating when the two species diverged genetically, scientists estimated that clothing appeared around 170,000 years ago, long before any physical garments survive.

faq.question: What evidence survives of prehistoric clothing?
faq.answer: Fabric and leather rarely survive, so evidence is indirect. Bone needles with eyelets, hide scrapers, and impressions on clay fragments suggest tailored garments. Ice Age figurines sometimes depict clothing details like caps and belts, providing visual evidence.
